examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Image of a Polygon Under the Action of a Linear Transformation
examples.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The triangle $\triangle ABC$ is shown below. Find $\triangle A'B'C',$ the image of $\triangle ABC$ under the action of $\mathbf T.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13990291/assets/4986bd2dab6b455c0d5e41909377c433d761bf7270364d3e2596e6db7f23981b.png)
examples.worked_solution:
To find the image of $T$ under the action of $\mathbf T,$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $\triangle ABC\mathbin{:}$

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 1 \\ -4 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of $\triangle A'B'C'$ are $(-3,-4), (0,0), (1,-2),$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13990291/assets/e8a14ffbaab4597a2a4a7c9a6bad61dabbc4970fc22c3ed2eb28b2594a670938.png)

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

A line segment $\overset{―}{YZ}$ has endpoints at $Y(2,-2)$ and $Z(0,1).$ What are the coordinates of the corresponding endpoints $\overset{―}{{Y}^{′}{Z}^{′}}$, the image of $\overset{―}{YZ}$ under the action of $T?$

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the image of $\overset{―}{YZ}$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the endpoints of $\overset{―}{YZ}:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective endpoints of the image are ${Y}^{′}(4,-4)$ and ${Z}^{′}(0,3).$
